thread.title: UPDATE: Amazon scammers headed to federal prison after $1.2 million fraud

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Amazon scammers headed to federal prison after $1.2 million fraud

organizations.name: u.s. attorney's office for the southern district of indiana

text:
By Tonya Garcia, MarketWatch
The trio profited from an elaborate consumer electronics scheme for years
Unlike some shoppers who say they were cut off from their Amazon.com Inc. accounts after a few returns, an Indiana husband-and-wife team was able to defraud the e-commerce giant for years before getting nabbed by authorities.
Erin and Leah Finan, both 38 years old, were sentenced to nearly six years in federal prison--71 months and 68 months, respectively--after the duo pleaded guilty to federal mail fraud and money laundering.
The couple and their accomplice, Danijel Glumac, a 29-year-old from Indianapolis, stole and sold more than 2,700 consumer electronics items, including GoPro Inc. (GPRO) cameras, Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) Surface tablets and Apple Inc. (AAPL) Macbooks, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Indiana.
Glumac pleaded guilty to money laundering and fencing the Finan's stolen goods across state lines. He was sentenced to two years in jail.
Read:Dick's Sporting Goods following Best Buy's 'playbook' after athletic-store bankruptcies (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dicks-sporting-goods-following-best-buys-playbook-after-athletic-store-bankruptcies-2018-05-31)
Between 2014 and 2017, the group repeatedly took advantage of Amazon's (AMZN) customer service policy (https://www.wsj.com/articles/banned-from-amazon-the-shoppers-who-make-too-many-returns-1526981401), claiming that items were damaged when they received them, and then requested free replacements. All told, the group stole more than $1.2 million in consumer electronics items.
The three were also ordered to pay full restitution.
"Consumer fraud not only unjustly enriches the perpetrator, it causes all of us to pay higher retail prices," said United States Attorney Josh Minkler in a statement. "To those who seek to exploit the convenience of online shopping through fraud, remember this case."
The Finans created "hundreds" of false identities to elude the company, placing "thousands" of orders and picking up the items from shipping locations across the state. Glumac bought more than 2,000 items from the Finans at marked up prices and sold them to a New York buyer, who then inflated the prices even higher to sell them to the public.
Oftentimes, the items were ultimately sold on Amazon, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office.
Don't miss: Best Buy's online sales have slowed, but should that cause concern? (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/best-buys-online-sales-have-slowed-but-should-that-cause-concern-2018-05-24)
The Finans made about $750,000 through the scheme. Glumac made nearly $500,000 after laundering the money through bank accounts tied to an apparel business.
The scam was uncovered through the efforts of the Indiana State Police, the Internal Revenue Service, and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, as well as the Department of Justice with input from Amazon.
"Shopping online has changed the way we think of retail," said Inspector in Charge Patricia Armstrong, of the Detroit Division, U.S. Postal Inspection Service. "Many of those purchases are shipped to consumers using the U.S. Mail. Postal Inspectors are proud to have partnered with fellow law enforcement to put an end to the illegal endeavors of these three criminals."
Also:There's one thing that people appear reluctant to buy on Amazon (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/theres-one-thing-people-appear-reluctant-to-buy-on-amazon-2018-06-06)
And:This is how Five Below sets itself apart from Amazon (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-is-how-five-below-sets-itself-apart-from-amazon-2018-06-07)
In addition to this scheme, the Finans also bounced checks, rented cars and houses that they never paid for, and committed other online fraud that involved selling rented softball equipment to parents on Facebook (FB), according to the U.S. Attorney's Office release.
Amazon shares are up nearly 67% for the past year while the S&P 500 index is up 14.2% for the period.
-Tonya Garcia;
